successors.note: Daemusin 'annexed Dongbuyeo and killed its king Daeso in 22 AD' (Daemusin page). The infobox also names Galsa Buyeo as a successor (no land, no date). A small state of Buyeo refugees revived the name about 285 (see buyeo).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; its Goguryeo shape of 23-42 does not cover this land). The page gives no capital, no area and no site beyond 'the land near to Okjeo'; the Goguryeo dossier's Yanji radius is kept for consistency. Capitals are omitted for the same reason.

ledger.note: 86 BCE: Hae Buru founds Eastern Buyeo by the sea. The Samguk sagi has Buru 'moved the capital eastward to the sea' and 'relocated to the land near to Okjeo'; 86 BCE is the start of Buru's reign in the infobox only. Rulers: Buru 86-48 BCE, Geumwa 48-7 BCE, Daeso 7 BCE-22 CE (infobox).

ledger.note: 22: Daemusin of Goguryeo kills King Daeso. 'He annexed Dongbuyeo and killed its king Daeso in 22 AD.' The Eastern Buyeo page has only that Daemusin 'attacked Dongbuyeo and killed King Daeso', that after internal strife its territory was absorbed, and 22 as the end of Daeso's reign.

notes: Short-lived (108 years) Buyeo offshoot. The refugee state of c. 285-410 that the Eastern Buyeo page calls a revival is carried in the buyeo dossier as its eastern branch (keyframe buyeo_285). The goguryeo dossier (jk-02-b) names 'buyeo' as counterpart of its 22 gain; it should name eastern-buyeo. No rulers strip because the Samguk sagi dates (Buru 86 BCE) rest on the infobox only and the page notes a chronology inconsistency in one legend.
